record.paper_title: On free curves and related open problems
record.context_brief: Rational cuspidal curves free or nearly free
record.original_question: Let C be a plane rational cuspidal curve, meaning an irreducible rational curve in P^2 whose singularities are all unibranch cusps. Must every such curve be either free or nearly free, where nearly free means that its freeness-defect invariant ν(C) equals 1?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1. Any plane rational cuspidal curve C is either free or nearly free.
A plane rational cuspidal curve is a rational curve C : f = 0 in the complex projective plane P2, having only unibranch singularities.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$ with homogeneous coordinates and let $C: f=0$ be a reduced plane curve of degree $d$ defined by a homogeneous polynomial $f \in S = \mathbb{C}[x,y,z]$. Let $J_f = (f_x, f_y, f_z)$ be the Jacobian ideal of $f$ and let $\mathrm{AR}(f) = \{(a,b,c) \in S^3 : a f_x + b f_y + c f_z = 0\}$ be the graded module of Jacobian syzygies (also called the module of derivations annihilating $f$).

The curve $C$ is said to be free if $\mathrm{AR}(f)$ is a free graded $S$-module of rank $2$; equivalently there exist integers $d_1 \le d_2$ with $d_1 + d_2 = d-1$ such that $\mathrm{AR}(f) \cong S(-d_1) \oplus S(-d_2)$. Define the freeness defect $\nu(C)$ as a nonnegative integer that measures how far $\mathrm{AR}(f)$ is from being free (with $\nu(C)=0$ iff $C$ is free). The curve $C$ is called nearly free if $\nu(C) = 1$.

A plane rational cuspidal curve is an irreducible curve $C \subset \mathbb{P}^2$ of geometric genus $0$ all of whose singularities are unibranch (i.e., each singular point has a single local analytic branch).

Question: Is it true that every plane rational cuspidal curve $C \subset \mathbb{P}^2$ is either free or nearly free?
artifact.category_tag: Free and nearly free plane curves
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (due to Dimca and Sticlaru) that every plane rational cuspidal curve is free or nearly free is known in many cases but is still open in general. It has been verified for curves of even degree, for curves of prime power degree, for curves whose fundamental group is abelian, for unicuspidal curves with a single Puiseux pair, and (by partial classification arguments) for many small-degree or small-rank cases (e.g., maximal multiplicity rank r ≤ 15 or degree d ≤ 90 with finitely many exceptions). The general statement remains unproven.

status_evidence.title: Nearly free divisors and rational cuspidal curves
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces nearly free divisors and formulates the conjecture that rational cuspidal plane curves are free or nearly free.
status_evidence.claim: Origin and formulation of the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: On rational cuspidal plane curves, and the local cohomology of Jacobian rings
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the conjecture in several special cases (even degree, prime power degree, abelian fundamental group).

status_evidence.title: On free curves and related open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture 5.1: Any plane rational cuspidal curve C is either free or nearly free.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open conjecture in a recent survey.
